subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on work done, power and efficiency, then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain efficiency and energy dissipation for GCSE Physics simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: A moving car has energy in which energy store?
questions.explain: Any moving object has energy in its kinetic store. The faster it moves and the greater its mass, the more energy is stored kinetically.

questions.q: A stretched spring stores energy in which store?
questions.explain: A stretched or compressed spring stores energy in its elastic potential store, released when the spring returns to its original shape.

questions.q: When a battery powers a torch bulb, energy is transferred mainly:
options: by heating from a hot object
electrically, then by light and heating radiation
questions.explain: The chemical store in the battery is transferred electrically to the bulb, which then transfers energy by light (radiation) and heating to the surroundings.

questions.q: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: can be destroyed but not created
is always lost during a transfer
can be created but not destroyed
cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or stored
questions.explain: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred between stores or dissipated. In a closed system the total energy stays the same.

questions.q: In a closed system, the total change in the total energy is:
options: equal to the useful energy only
questions.explain: In a closed system there is no net change in the total energy: energy is transferred between stores but none enters or leaves, so the total stays constant.

questions.q: Which statement about work done is correct?
options: Work is only done when an object is stationary
Work done equals the energy transferred and is measured in joules
Work done is measured in newtons
Work done equals force divided by distance
questions.explain: Work done (in joules) equals the energy transferred. Work is done whenever a force moves an object in the direction of the force: W = F x d.

questions.q: A force of 50 N pushes a box 4 m along the floor in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explain: Work done = force x distance = 50 N x 4 m = 200 J. Work is measured in joules, not newtons.

questions.q: A crane does 6000 J of work lifting a load with a force of 300 N. How far does it lift the load?
questions.explain: Rearrange W = F x d to d = W / F = 6000 / 300 = 20 m.

questions.q: A person pushes hard against a heavy wall that does not move. How much work is done on the wall?
options: Zero, because the wall does not move any distance
questions.explain: Work done = force x distance moved in the direction of the force. If the wall does not move, distance = 0, so no work is done on it, however large the force.

questions.q: A 2 kg mass is raised 3 m. Using g = 10 N/kg, how much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
questions.explain: Change in GPE = m x g x h = 2 kg x 10 N/kg x 3 m = 60 J.

questions.q: A 4 kg object moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
If the speed of a moving object doubles (mass unchanged), its kinetic energy:
questions.explain: KE depends on speed squared (KE = 1/2 m v^2). Doubling the speed multiplies v^2 by 4, so the kinetic energy becomes four times greater.

questions.q: Power is best defined as:
options: the force needed to move an object
the rate at which energy is transferred (or work is done)
the total energy stored in a system
questions.explain: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred or work is done. It is measured in watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

questions.q: A motor transfers 600 J of energy in 30 s. What is its power?
questions.explain: Power = energy transferred / time = 600 J / 30 s = 20 W.

questions.q: Machine A does 1000 J of work in 10 s. Machine B does 1000 J of work in 20 s. Which is more powerful and why?
options: Machine B, because it takes longer
Machine B, because it does more work
Machine A, because it transfers the same energy in less time
questions.explain: Power = work done / time. A: 1000/10 = 100 W. B: 1000/20 = 50 W. Machine A transfers the same energy in less time, so it is more powerful.

questions.q: Which equation gives the efficiency of a device?
options: efficiency = useful power output x total power input
efficiency = useful energy transferred by the device / total energy supplied to the device
efficiency = total energy input / useful energy output
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful energy transferred by the device / total energy supplied to the device. It can also be written using power, and is a ratio (often given as a percentage).

questions.q: A device is supplied with 200 J of energy and usefully transfers 40 J. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful / total = 40 / 200 = 0.2 = 20%.

questions.q: Why is no ordinary machine ever 100% efficient?
options: Because energy is destroyed inside it
Because the useful output is always greater than the input
Because it always creates extra energy
Because some energy is always dissipated to the surroundings, usually by heating
questions.explain: Some energy is always dissipated (spread out) to the surroundings, usually as heat, often due to friction. This wasted energy is stored in less useful ways, so efficiency is always below 100%.

questions.q: Which method reduces energy wasted through friction in a machine's moving parts?
options: Lubricating the moving parts with oil
questions.explain: Lubricating moving parts with oil reduces friction, so less energy is dissipated as heat. This makes the machine more efficient.

questions.q: A lamp is supplied with 100 J of energy. It gives out 15 J as light and the rest as heat. How much energy is dissipated (wasted) as heat?
questions.explain: By conservation of energy, wasted energy = total supplied - useful output = 100 J - 15 J = 85 J dissipated as heat.
